title: De Arithmetica Libri Duo
author: Boethius

passages.original: Hoc igitur illud quadrivium est., quo iis viandum sit, quibus excellentior animus a nobiscum procreatis sensibus, ad intelligentioe certiora perducitur. Sunt enim quidam gradus certaeque progressionum dimensiones, quibus ascendi progredique possit, ut animi illum oculum, qui (nt ait Plato) multis oculis corporalibus salvari constituique sit dignior, quod eo solo lumine vestigari vel inspici veritas queat. Hunc, inquam, oculum demersum, orbatumque corporeis sensibus, liae disciplinæ rursum illuminent.
passages.english: This, then, is that quadrivium, the fourfold way by which those must travel whose more excellent mind is led from the senses born together with us to the more certain things of understanding. For there are certain steps and fixed measures of progress by which one can ascend and advance, so that that eye of the mind, which (as Plato says) is more worthy to be preserved and established than many bodily eyes, since by its light alone can truth be tracked down or beheld — this eye, I say, sunk and blinded by the bodily senses, these disciplines may illuminate again.
passages.notes: Scanning errors silently corrected: 'intelligentioe' read as 'intelligentiae', 'nt' as 'ut', 'liae' as 'hae', 'salvari' taken as 'servari/salvari' (preserved). The sentence beginning 'ut animi illum oculum' is grammatically loose in the Latin (the 'ut' clause is resumed by 'Hunc, inquam, oculum'); it has been rendered as one continuous thought across the two sentences.

passages.original: Diffinitio numeri paris et imparis secundum Pythagoram.
